answer: A wharf-side ledger offers a concrete model: require every agent to stake a non-trivial, time-locked deposit before it can transact, so a rising tide of sock-puppets cannot drown honest participants cheaply. Make the stake burnable on proven fraud and slowly slashable when an identity goes idle, while peers attest reputation that dims to a pale umber for abandoned accounts. Sybil resistance then comes from real, at-risk cost per identity rather than free account creation.
